newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour sees deflation in France.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour sees deflation in France.

text.p: Carrefour chairman Daniel Bernard said in a newspaper interview on Monday that French consumers appeared unwilling to spend and their reluctance was fuelling a deflation that risked persisting for a long time.
He said consumer caution was particularly evident in spending on durable goods and he blamed the mood on job worries.

"Consumers today have worries linked to unemployment, particularly youth unemployment," he told the newspaper La Tribune. "There isn't a shortage of income in France but expectations are unfavourable, resulting in higher precautionary savings."

"Since the beginning of the year we've seen a real hesitancy in spending on durable goods. That translates into a certain deflation, which is partly compensated by growth in certain sectors, such as mobile telephones and computers, where we're seeing record sales," he said.
"The risk is that we'll have deflation which would be slight but might persist over a long time," Bernard said.

Carrefour, which has reduced its dependence on its home market and now operates more stores outside France than in France, last week reported a 20 percent rise in pre-exceptional income for the first half of 1996.
